question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(t)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{h}^{5}-32{h}^{4}-4{h}^{3} & =16{h}^{3}-13{h}^{5} \\ 16{h}^{5}-32{h}^{4}-4{h}^{3} & =16{h}^{3} \\ 16{h}^{5}-32{h}^{4}-20{h}^{3} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $4{h}^{3}.$ We can factor out the $4{h}^{3}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{h}^{5}-32{h}^{4}-20{h}^{3} & =0 \\ 4{h}^{3}(4{h}^{2}-8h-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $4{h}^{2}-8h-5$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{h}^{3}(4{h}^{2}-8h-5) & =0 \\ 4{h}^{3}(2h+1)(2h-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $h=0,$ $h=-\frac{1}{2},$ and $h=\frac{5}{2}.$
